A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VAPT research. All 55 pages of v1 and 57 pages of v4, including Appendices A–E, support comparison; rendered inspection resolves extraction issues in equations and plot labels.

before.justification: v1 reports original FGVC and VTAB-1K classification experiments, sample-efficiency results, ablations, computational measurements, and visualizations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same token-wise projectors, channel-wise convolution, shared feature projector with ReLU, LayerNorm, and adaptive prompts inserted into ViT blocks. The proof revisions do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet pretraining coverage and evaluate five FGVC and nineteen VTAB-1K classification tasks. The Stanford Dogs subsampling, CUB backbone-scaling, and selected-task sensitivity and visualization scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within corresponding experiments. Table 1 retains LoRA and E2VPT among its baselines, Table 2 retains GateVPT, and the appendix comparisons retain their respective methods.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D retain the reported splits, augmentation, hyperparameter grids, batch sizes, 100-epoch SGD schedule, and accuracy metrics. The Stanford Dogs subsampling and epoch-rescaling protocol and backbone configurations also match.

E4.justification: The component, sharing, convolution, linear-activation, and hyperparameter analyses in Appendix E are unchanged. Backbone scaling, sample efficiency, computational comparisons, and GradCAM cases are also retained; relocated figures do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 still specifies three runs, and Appendix E.1 still describes different initialization seeds and standard-deviation error bars. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The numerical and visual results match. Table 1 retains VAPT's 72.91 VTAB-1K mean and 89.58 FGVC accuracy; Table 3 retains 60.1 versus 3.6 at 1% Stanford Dogs training data. Appendix scores, parameter counts, costs, and plotted findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The theorems, assumptions, losses, and convergence rates remain unchanged. Limited proof corrections include replacing the strict limiting inequality with >= epsilon' in the compactness arguments and distinguishing actual atom count from L'. However, Appendix B also introduces a reversed matrix product and D1/D2 inconsistencies.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: identifying input-invariant prompts' limited expressiveness, proposing VAPT, claiming optimal sample efficiency, and reporting stronger performance with fewer parameters.

C2.justification: The explanations involving global information, spatial relationships, projector sharing, and improved localization are retained. The conclusion still limits the investigation to ViT architectures and classification, with the same proposed extensions.

D1.justification: Appendix D retains the implementation, preprocessing, hyperparameter ranges, optimizer settings, PyTorch framework, and NVIDIA A100-40GB hardware information. Both versions promise future implementation availability without adding access instructions.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds Nguyen, Akbarian, and Ho's 'Is temperature sample efficient for softmax Gaussian mixture of experts?' to the convergence-rate discussion. The remaining literature coverage and positioning relative to VPT and MoE research are retained.

P1.justification: Appendices A.1 and B extensively rewrite proof narration, expanding explanations of Taylor expansions, coefficient arguments, and limiting steps. Appendix B gains explicit local/global subheadings. Main-text wording receives smaller edits, including the affiliation change from VinAI Research to Movian AI, Vietnam.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained. Figure 6 moves from beside the backbone-scaling discussion to the later figure pages; Figure 9 now shares a page with Figure 10 instead of Figures 7–8. Equations and appendix text reflow without a substantial display redesign.

improvement.justification: More explicit proof explanations and the corrected compactness inequality coexist with new formula inconsistencies. Appendix B replaces D2n with D1n in one passage and reverses the matrix product defining G'_n (v4 pages 34 and 37). With the method and empirical evidence unchanged, the competing effects on proof readability and precision leave the net quality change uncertain.
